subject: Navvana POC: language fallback strategy, eval rubric, and timeline
content:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Linh Tran <linh.tran@navvana.com>, Ravi Kapoor <ravi.kapoor@navvana.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Oct 2028 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Navvana POC: language fallback strategy, eval rubric, and timeline

Hi Linh / Ravi —

Thanks again for the time earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single artefact to iterate on. We captured a lot in the call; below is a compact POC charter and ownership map so everyone can align before we draft the SOW.

Objective:
- Validate that Redwood's hosted inference can meet Navvana's multilingual support needs for customer-facing chat and triage (EN/VI/JP).
- Verify latency, hallucination rates, and slot-level extraction accuracy against your sample logs.

Success criteria (proposed):
- 95th percentile reply time <= 750ms for EN, <= 900ms for VI/JP at baseline concurrency (50 concurrent chats).
- Intent classification accuracy >= 92% (measured F1 on your labeled set).
- Hallucination occurrences <= 0.8% (measured via sampling + manual review threshold you suggested).
- End-to-end token cost per session within the target we discussed (we'll model this in the trial).

Evaluation plan & metrics:
- Redwood to run a 2-week controlled trial with your anonymized sample conversations.
- We will run automated regressions and a small human-review panel for hallucination checks.
- Primary metrics: p95 latency, per-intent F1, hallucination rate, token cost per 1k messages, and throughput at 50/150 concurrent sessions.
- Acceptance is met when all criteria are within thresholds on the same 48-hour window and no critical stability incidents.

Model selection (trial recommendations):
- Primary pick: Mistral-style instruction-tuned 7B (strong latency/cost balance for EN + VI where local LMs perform well).
- Secondary pick (fallback/high-quality): Llama3-13B instruction variant (quantized int4) for JP/edge cases where quality is prioritized.
- Canary/fallback policy: route to Llama3 variant for queries flagged with low-confidence by the confidence detector; otherwise serve Mistral-style model.
- Multilingual routing: a lightweight language classifier (client-side) sends a lang tag; Redwood routing will favor the model variant tuned for that language.

Data residency & security notes:
- For this hosted POC we'll accept anonymized transcripts; Redwood will sign an NDA supplement and follow your data-retention window (14 days for POC logs).
- SRE audit: we will provide read-only limited logs and an access matrix document attached.

Timeline (proposed):
- Week 0 (this week): finalize SOW + grant test dataset access (Navvana) — owners: Priya (sales), Ravi (Navvana).
- Week 1: Instance provisioning + model config + baseline smoke tests — owner: Ben (SE).
- Week 2: Run batch evaluation across sample set; start human review for hallucination cases — owners: Ben + Navvana data lead.
- Week 3: Performance ramp tests (50 -> 150 concurrent) + acceptance check-in — owner: Ben.
- Week 4: Final acceptance review and handoff to operations for production onboarding conversation — owner: Priya/Ben.

Attachments: I attached a draft SOW and a sample eval rubric to speed sign-off. I also linked the HubSpot deal and a Drive folder where we'll place test artifacts.

Next steps for immediate action items:
1) Navvana: share sanitized sample set and confirm the test account for S3 access by EOD Thu.
2) Redwood: send final SOW (attached) and calendar invites for kickoff.
3) Ben: prepare model config matrix and initial routing rules for review on Thu sync.

If this looks good I'll push the SOW and kick off the calendar invites.

Thanks —
Priya
Priya Natarajan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
priay.natarajan@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0133

From: Linh Tran <linh.tran@navvana.com>

Date: Tue, 11 Oct 2028 11:05:00 +0700
Subject: Re: Navvana POC: language fallback strategy, eval rubric, and timeline

Hi Priya —

Thanks for the recap. A few clarifications from our side before we finalize the SOW: 
- For Japanese (JP) traffic ~12% of queries are technical support with domain-specific tokens (product names, error codes). We want to prioritize quality there, so routing to the Llama3-13B variant for low-confidence/potential hallucination cases makes sense.
- For Vietnamese (VI) the main issue is idiomatic phrasing — we want to ensure the language model doesn't force literal translations. If Mistral-style 7B shows issues we'll accept fallback to an ensembled approach for the trial (one pass with 7B + quick rerank by Llama3-13B for top-2 responses).
- Regarding metrics: can Redwood provide a small dashboard with daily p95 latency + hallucination sample rate? That will help our PM/ops review.

We'll aim to share the sanitized set by Thu. I also attached our internal labeling guide (sensitive fields redacted) — please confirm you received it.

Best,
Linh
Linh Tran
Head of AI Product, Navvana
linh.tran@navvana.com

> Quick technical plan + what I'll deliver by Friday:

> 1) Model config matrix (attached to SOW folder): exact model names, tokenization notes, quantization plan (int4 on Llama3-13B), and inference knobs (max_new_tokens, temp scheduling, top_k) tuned per-language.
>
> 2) Routing rules: simple confidence threshold (0.6) -> fallback to Llama3; language tag route -> prefer Llama3 for JP, allow Mistral-style for EN/VI by default. I'll include pseudo-code for the routing policy and the canary fallback (route x% to Llama3 for the first 24 hours).
>
> 3) Dashboard endpoints: daily p95 latency, hourly hallucination sample rate (random 500 samples/day), intent F1 (daily), token-cost estimator. I'll provide a CSV export and a small Grafana dashboard in the Drive link.
>
> Notes on ensemble approach for VI: we can do fast 7B inference + 13B rerank for top-2 on the first pass. Latency impact will be measurable — I will include expected p95 delta and a togglable rerank flag in the config.
>
> Security/ops: I will drop an access matrix and the minimal logs export schema (only anonymized utterance id + timestamps + model tag + confidence).
>
> Deliverables by Fri EOD (Ben): model matrix, routing pseudo-code, dashboard endpoints + sample CSV, and a test-run checklist.
>

> Ben
